ranking_by: surface gravity (cloud-top level for gas giants)
title: The 5 Planets With the Strongest Gravity, Ranked (Earth Is #4)

scenes.text: Earth makes the top five. And one planet beats it by more than double.

scenes.label: Venus · 8.9 m/s²
scenes.text: Number five: Venus. Gravity about nine tenths of Earth's, so you'd feel a little lighter.

scenes.label: Earth · 9.8 m/s²
scenes.text: Number four: Earth. Our own gravity, the baseline for every other planet.

scenes.label: Saturn · 10.4 m/s²
scenes.text: Number three: Saturn. Ninety-five times Earth's mass, yet only about six percent stronger gravity at its cloud tops.

scenes.label: Neptune · 11.2 m/s²
scenes.text: Number two: Neptune. About fourteen percent stronger than Earth's, measured at the cloud tops.

scenes.label: Jupiter · 24.8 m/s²
scenes.text: Number one: Jupiter. Two and a half times Earth's gravity. You'd weigh over twice as much.

description:
The five planets with the strongest surface gravity, with gas giants measured at their cloud tops.
Jupiter is number one by a mile, and Earth beats Venus, Uranus, Mars and Mercury.
Which planet would you most like to stand on?
first_comment: Would you rather weigh double on Jupiter or float on Mars? And what should we rank next?
